posts.style: Design & Aspiration · The Court Below the House
posts.alt: An Olivenhain estate backyard at golden hour behind a white board-and-batten modern farmhouse with a dark standing-seam roof: a green and slate VersaCourt sport court sunk below a stacked-stone wall, wide travertine steps up to a louvered cabana with teak lounge seating and a built-in grill, olive trees, native grasses and agave, with neighboring estate homes, barns and fenced pastures visible close by across the hills
posts.hook: On an estate lot, the question isn't what fits. It's what deserves the best ground.
posts.caption:
Most big yards spread everything out and nothing ends up feeling connected. This one is cut into terraces, so each level has one job and the view runs through all of them.

The court sits a few feet below the house, held by a stacked-stone wall, so from the kitchen it reads as a green field instead of a fence line. One flight of wide steps up is the cabana: a louvered shade structure over a lounge and a built-in grill, close enough to call a game and still be at the table. Olive trees and native grasses soften the edges and tie it back to the hills.

The selections:
• VersaCourt sport court · pickleball and tennis lines
• Eldorado Stone retaining and seat walls
• StruXure louvered cabana with Lynx built-in grill
• silver travertine terrace & steps
• olive trees, deer grass & agave · FX Luminaire path lighting

posts.style: Neighborhood · Driveway & Curb Appeal · Slabs and Turf Joints
posts.alt: The front yard of a single-story 1980s contemporary ranch home in Scripps Ranch at golden hour: warm grey stucco with vertical cedar siding, a driveway of large slate-textured Techo-Bloc slabs in a staggered run with narrow turf joints, a matching walk to the front door, feather grass, blue agave, kangaroo paw and bougainvillea in decomposed granite, bronze path lights, tall eucalyptus and neighboring homes visible close by down the street
posts.hook: A driveway doesn't have to be a slab of grey. It can be the best part of the front yard.
posts.caption:
Scripps Ranch homes were built with the eucalyptus in mind, and the best front yards still take their cue from the trees: warm wood, soft grasses, long low lines.

This driveway follows that lead. Large slate-textured slabs set in a staggered run, with narrow ribbons of turf between them, so the drive reads as a pattern instead of a parking pad. The same slabs step up to the front door. Around them the lawn gave way to decomposed granite, feather grass, blue agave, kangaroo paw and bougainvillea, which looks this good in December and most of the year.

Curb appeal is the first room of the house. Treat it like one.

The selections:
• Techo-Bloc Blu 60 slate-texture slabs · driveway & entry walk
• SYNLawn turf ribbons between the slabs
• Mexican feather grass, blue agave, kangaroo paw & bougainvillea in decomposed granite
• Kichler bronze path lights

Want a front yard that earns a second look from the street? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.style: Craft & Process · The Hillside That Became Two Rooms
posts.alt: A compact tiered backyard behind a white 1920s Spanish bungalow in Mission Hills at golden hour: a copper water bowl spilling into a basin on the upper terrace, wide stone steps with bullnose treads, stacked-stone retaining and seat walls, a paver patio with two teak loungers under citrus trees, bougainvillea, bird of paradise, agave and lavender, with neighboring craftsman and Spanish homes visible close by over the wood fences
posts.hook: A small sloped lot has one advantage most flat yards never get: levels.
posts.caption:
Mission Hills lots are tight, and a lot of them tilt. The temptation is to flatten everything and pour a patio. The better move is to keep the grade and build with it.

Here the slope became two rooms. The upper terrace holds a water bowl that spills into a small basin, so there's sound at the door. Wide stone steps bring you down to a paver patio with room for two loungers under the citrus. The stacked-stone walls do the structural work and double as seating, and the planting is the kind that thrives on a dry San Diego hillside: bougainvillea, bird of paradise, agave and lavender.

Most of what makes this work you can't see: compacted base, drainage behind every wall, footings sized for the hill. That's the part we obsess over.

The selections:
• Eldorado Stone stacked-stone retaining & seat walls
• Belgard Dimensions steps with bullnose treads
• Acker-Stone paver patio
• Bobe copper water bowl with basin spill
• citrus, bougainvillea, bird of paradise & lavender · FX Luminaire wall-wash lights

Have a slope you've been working around for years? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.style: Lifestyle · Seasonal · The December Dinner Outside
posts.alt: A Rancho Penasquitos family backyard at dusk in December behind a two-story grey stucco tract home with brick wainscot and glowing windows: a bronze pergola with string lights over a long teak dining table set for dinner, a sand-blend paver patio, a stone fire pit lit in the corner beside a turf lawn, raised block planters with lavender, olive and agave, and neighboring two-story homes visible close by beyond the wood fence
posts.hook: In San Diego the December dinner table can still be outside. It just needs a roof and a little warmth.
posts.caption:
Most of the country packs the patio furniture away by now. Here, the cool evenings are the best ones, as long as the yard was built for them.

This one was. A pergola holds the dining table close to the kitchen door, with string lights overhead and a wall sconce for the walk inside. A fire pit in the corner keeps the lawn side warm once the plates are cleared, and the turf stays green for whoever is still running around after dinner. Raised block planters of lavender, olive and agave frame the patio without crowding it.

Nothing exotic. Just a yard that doesn't close for the season.

The selections:
• Trex Pergola in bronze with string lighting
• Belgard Urbana paver patio
• Warming Trends fire pit with stone veneer surround
• SYNLawn turf lawn
• olive, lavender & agave in raised planters · FX Luminaire path lights

Want a dining room with no walls and no season? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.style: Trust & Difference · The Winter Design Window
posts.alt: A Poway backyard at golden hour behind a single-story stone-base ranch home: a louvered pergola over an outdoor kitchen with a stone veneer island, built-in grill and bar seating, an ivory porcelain patio, a rectangular pool with a raised stone wall, turf panels, olive trees, agave and ornamental grasses, with neighboring ranch homes visible close by beyond the fence and across the chaparral valley
posts.hook: The yards that are ready by the first long evenings of May are designed now.
posts.caption:
We schedule months out on purpose. Design comes first, then selections, then permits where they're needed, then a crew that shows up with every decision already made.

In practice that means December and January are when the spring projects are drawn. The pool, the kitchen island, the louvered pergola and the planting all get resolved on paper while the yard is still quiet. By the time we break ground, the plan is finished and the materials are ordered.

That's what “by design, not by dispatch” means. Nobody is figuring it out in the field, and nobody is waiting on us in June.

The selections:
• StruXure louvered pergola over the kitchen
• Eldorado Stone kitchen island with Lynx built-in grill & bar
• Belgard Porcelain patio in ivory
• rectangular pool with a raised stone wall
• SYNLawn turf, olive & ornamental grasses · Kichler path lighting

Thinking about spring? Winter is when it gets designed. DM “DESIGN”.
